components.note: 生 (birth) — traditional 產 was 生 (birth) topped by 彦 for sound; the idea is giving birth, so bringing forth, as in 生产 and 产生.

example.hanzi: 这家工厂每天生产一千台电视。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng měitiān shēngchǎn yìqiān tái diànshì.
example.english: This factory produces a thousand TVs every day.
example.fact: 产 is used in compounds rather than alone: 生产 (to manufacture), 产品 (product), 财产 (property), 产生 (to arise). It also means childbirth: 产假 is maternity leave and 产妇 is a woman in labor.

examples.hanzi: 这个地区出产很多茶叶。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dìqū chūchǎn hěn duō cháyè.
examples.english: This region produces a lot of tea.

examples.hanzi: 这家店只卖本地的土特产。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn zhǐ mài běndì de tǔtèchǎn.
examples.english: This shop only sells local specialties.

components.note: 重 (zhòng) is a sound clue for 种 zhǒng/zhòng; it means heavy (zhòng) or to repeat (chóng, as in 重新).
廴 (long stride) — a rare radical of walking and extending, also in 延 yán and 廷 tíng; 建 means to set up or put up; the sound clue 聿 is only loose.

example.hanzi: 战后，这座城市花了十年重建。
example.pinyin: Zhàn hòu, zhè zuò chéngshì huāle shí nián chóngjiàn.
example.english: After the war, this city spent ten years rebuilding.
example.fact: After World War II left Warsaw's Old Town almost completely destroyed, Polish architects rebuilt it brick by brick between 1949 and 1963 using pre-war photographs, measured drawings, and even 18th-century paintings by the Venetian artist Bernardo Bellotto as reference. UNESCO later added the reconstructed district to its World Heritage List specifically because of the scale and precision of that restoration effort.

examples.hanzi: 这座古桥在去年被重建了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔqiáo zài qùnián bèi chóngjiàn le.
examples.english: This old bridge was rebuilt last year.

examples.hanzi: 灾后重建需要很多时间。
examples.pinyin: Zāihòu chóngjiàn xūyào hěn duō shíjiān.
examples.english: Rebuilding after a disaster takes a lot of time.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 按; 批 is to strike, then to comment.
比 (bǐ) is a loose hint for pī.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talk: 说, 论, 请; 评 is to comment and judge.
平 (píng) sounds exactly like 评; also in 苹 píng.

example.hanzi: 老师严厉地批评了他的作业。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī yánlì de pīpíngle tā de zuòyè.
example.english: The teacher harshly criticized his homework.
example.fact: The Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society, first published in 1665, is credited with introducing formal peer review to scientific publishing, requiring that submitted papers be checked and criticized by other experts before appearing in print. That practice of routine expert criticism became the backbone of how scientific claims are still vetted today.

examples.hanzi: 别批评孩子，多鼓励他。
examples.pinyin: Bié pīpíng háizi, duō gǔlì tā.
examples.english: Don't criticize the child, and encourage him more.

examples.hanzi: 她对这部电影提出了批评。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhè bù diànyǐng tíchū le pīpíng.
examples.english: She offered criticism of this movie.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 大家都说是他先动手的。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu shuōshì tā xiān dòngshǒu de.
example.english: Everyone says that he was the one who struck first.
example.fact: In the childhood game known as “telephone” or “Chinese whispers,” a short message whispered from person to person along a chain reliably comes out garbled by the end, even in groups of only a dozen people. Psychologists studying rumor transmission have used the same setup to show how each retelling tends to sharpen a few dramatic details while dropping nuance, a pattern also seen in how rumors spread through real communities.

examples.hanzi: 他说是你告诉他的。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō shì nǐ gàosu tā de.
examples.english: He said it was you who told him.

examples.hanzi: 说是明天会下雪，不知道是真的吗？
examples.pinyin: Shuōshì míngtiān huì xiàxuě, bù zhīdào shì zhēn de ma?
examples.english: It's said that it will snow tomorrow, but is that true?

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 深 is deep water.
罙 (shēn) — same sound — 深 is shēn; 罙 also sounds out 探 tàn.
入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.

example.hanzi: 科学家们深入研究了这种病毒。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen shēnrù yánjiūle zhè zhǒng bìngdú.
example.english: The scientists studied this virus in depth.
example.fact: The Challenger Deep, located in the Mariana Trench in the western Pacific, plunges to about 10,935 meters below sea level, making it the deepest known point in any of Earth's oceans. Only a handful of crewed vehicles, starting with the Trieste in 1960 and including James Cameron's 2012 solo dive, have ever reached its floor.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要深入了解客户的想法。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào shēnrù liǎojiě kèhù de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: We need a deep understanding of the customers' thinking.

examples.hanzi: 他们深入森林寻找失踪的人。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shēnrù sēnlín xúnzhǎo shīzōng de rén.
examples.english: They went deep into the forest to look for the missing person.

components.note: 尺 (ruler) — the main part, as in 尺寸 size. Dictionary story: a place where measures are discussed (口), like a bureau; 局 also means 'game' as in 结局.
口 (mouth/box) — placed inside 尺. It represents talk or a space; Memory aid: a ruler fitted to a mouth means rules are discussed in an 'office'.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.hanzi: 谈判陷入了僵持的局面。
example.pinyin: Tánpàn xiànrùle jiāngchí de júmiàn.
example.english: The negotiation fell into a deadlocked situation.
example.fact: During the Cuban Missile Crisis in October 1962, the United States and the Soviet Union came within what historians widely regard as the closest the Cold War ever came to nuclear war, after American reconnaissance flights discovered Soviet missile sites being built in Cuba. The standoff was resolved within thirteen days through secret negotiations in which the U.S. quietly agreed not to invade Cuba in exchange for the missiles' removal.

examples.hanzi: 比赛进入了激烈的局面。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài jìnrù le jīliè de júmiàn.
examples.english: The match entered an intense stage.

examples.hanzi: 新政策改变了市场的局面。
examples.pinyin: Xīn zhèngcè gǎibiàn le shìchǎng de júmiàn.
examples.english: The new policy changed the market situation.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 操 is to handle or drill.
喿 (zào) hints at the sound: 操 cāo is close to 澡 zǎo and 燥 zào.
纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — thread and rein; 纵 is to let loose, as in 红 red, 级 level.
从 (cóng) rhymes loosely with zòng.

example.hanzi: 飞行员通过操纵杆操纵飞机。
example.pinyin: Fēixíngyuán tōngguò cāozònggǎn cāozòng fēijī.
example.english: The pilot operates the aircraft using the control stick.
example.fact: Modern airliners increasingly use fly-by-wire systems, in which a pilot's movements of the control stick are converted into electronic signals that a computer interprets before adjusting the control surfaces, rather than moving them through direct mechanical linkages. Airbus introduced the first commercial fly-by-wire jet, the A320, in 1988, and the approach is now standard across most large modern aircraft.

examples.hanzi: 有人在背后操纵这件事。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén zài bèihòu cāozòng zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: Someone is manipulating this matter behind the scenes.

examples.hanzi: 小孩正在用遥控器操纵玩具车。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái zhèngzài yòng yáokòngqì cāozòng wánjù chē.
examples.english: The child is steering a toy car with a remote.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 逃 is to run away.
兆 (zhào) — loose hint — 逃 is táo; 兆 also sounds out 桃 táo (same sound) and 跳 tiào.
離 (traditional) — 隹 (bird) plus 离 as sound (lí). 离 was an old name for a mythical beast, so the 'leave' sense comes from 離; 离 kept only the sound part.

example.hanzi: 他们连夜逃离了着火的房子。
example.pinyin: Tāmen liányè táolíle zháohuǒ de fángzi.
example.english: They fled the burning house in the middle of the night.
example.fact: In June 1962, three inmates, Frank Morris and brothers John and Clarence Anglin, escaped from the supposedly inescapable Alcatraz federal prison by chiseling through the walls of their cells with sharpened spoons and paddling away on a raft made from raincoats. Despite an extensive FBI manhunt, none of the three were ever conclusively found, and the case remains officially unsolved.

examples.hanzi: 小鸟逃离了笼子。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo niǎo táolí le lóngzi.
examples.english: The little bird escaped from the cage.

examples.hanzi: 他一直想逃离这个小城市。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìzhí xiǎng táolí zhège xiǎo chéngshì.
examples.english: He has always wanted to escape this small town.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and waves: 河, 海, 汤; 浪 is a wave.
良 (liáng) is a loose clue; also in 狼 láng, 朗 lǎng and 娘 niáng.

example.hanzi: 海上的浪很大。
example.pinyin: Hǎi shàng de làng hěn dà.
example.english: The waves on the sea are big.
example.fact: 浪 means a wave, and from the restless sea came the sense "roaming" or "unrestrained": 流浪 (to wander), 浪费 (to waste). In slang, 浪 means to go out and have wild fun: 出去浪.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢在海边看浪花。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài hǎibiān kàn lànghuā.
examples.english: I like watching the waves at the seaside.

examples.hanzi: 别浪费时间了，快点儿做吧。
examples.pinyin: Bié làngfèi shíjiān le, kuài diǎnr zuò ba.
examples.english: Don't waste time, do it quickly.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talking: 说, 计, 谈; 设 is to set up or plan by instruction.
殳 (shū, hand holding a tool) is only a loose sound clue; also in 投 tóu and 股 gǔ.
罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and catching: 罗, 罚, 罪; 置 first meant to set a net, then to place.
直 (zhí) is a near sound match for zhì; same part in 值 zhí and 植 zhí.

example.hanzi: 请在手机里设置一个新密码。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài shǒujī lǐ shèzhì yí gè xīn mìmǎ.
example.english: Please set up a new password on your phone.
example.fact: The world's first electric traffic signal was installed at a junction in London in 1868, designed by railway engineer J. P. Knight and operated manually by a police constable who raised colored semaphore arms and lit gas lamps at night. It exploded within weeks after a gas leak injured the officer operating it, and traffic signals did not reappear widely until automated electric versions spread through American cities in the 1910s.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我设置一下闹钟。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ shèzhì yíxià nàozhōng.
examples.english: Please help me set the alarm.

examples.hanzi: 这个软件的设置很简单。
examples.pinyin: Zhège ruǎnjiàn de shèzhì hěn jiǎndān.
examples.english: This software's settings are very simple.

components.note: 回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.
广 (building, shelter) — the roof-and-wall frame, as in 店, 床, 度. Here it is mostly the outline of the old 應.
心 (heart) — hidden in the traditional 應, 'respond from the heart'; simplification dropped it. 应 is yīng (should) or yìng (respond).

example.hanzi: 公司还没有对这条消息做出回应。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī hái méiyǒu duì zhè tiáo xiāoxi zuòchū huíyìng.
example.english: The company has not yet responded to this piece of news.
example.fact: Bats navigate and hunt in complete darkness using echolocation, emitting rapid ultrasonic clicks and interpreting the timing and pitch of the echoes that bounce back off nearby objects and insects. Some species can detect prey as thin as a human hair and adjust their calls in real time depending on how cluttered or open their surroundings are.

examples.hanzi: 对于我的建议，他没有回应。
examples.pinyin: Duìyú wǒ de jiànyì, tā méiyǒu huíyìng.
examples.english: He didn't respond to my suggestion.

examples.hanzi: 观众热烈地回应了演员的问候。
examples.pinyin: Guānzhòng rèliè de huíyìng le yǎnyuán de wènhòu.
examples.english: The audience responded warmly to the actor's greeting.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 滚 is to roll like boiling water.
衮 (gǔn) — same sound — 滚 is gǔn, like 衮.
虫 (insect, creature) — small animals and insects, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蛇 snake, 虾 shrimp: 蛋 is the egg of a creature.

example.hanzi: 他生气地喊道：“你给我滚蛋！”
example.pinyin: Tā shēngqì de hǎndào: “Nǐ gěi wǒ gǔndàn!”
example.english: He shouted angrily, “Get out of here!”
example.fact: Tumbleweeds, most commonly the plant Salsola tragus in North America, are not native to the continent at all; they arrived accidentally from Eurasia with contaminated grain shipments in the 1870s. Once the plant dries out and its stem snaps at the base, wind sends the whole rounded skeleton rolling across open ground, scattering thousands of seeds along the way.

examples.hanzi: 别再烦我了，滚蛋！
examples.pinyin: Bié zài fán wǒ le, gǔndàn!
examples.english: Stop bothering me, get lost!

examples.hanzi: 他被老板骂了一句滚蛋。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi lǎobǎn mà le yí jù gǔndàn.
examples.english: The boss yelled at him to get out.

components.note: 夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.
Memory aid: 业 looks like a row of upright posts on a base, like a shop sign or an old tool stand; 'business/trade' is the extended meaning. Origin is unclear, so no firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 疫情期间，很多人都失业了。
example.pinyin: Yìqíng qījiān, hěnduō rén dōu shīyè le.
example.english: During the pandemic, many people lost their jobs.
example.fact: At the depth of the Great Depression in 1933, the unemployment rate in the United States reached roughly 25 percent, meaning one in four workers had no job. It took nearly a decade of New Deal programs and, ultimately, the industrial mobilization for World War II before employment returned to pre-Depression levels.

examples.hanzi: 他因为公司倒闭而失业了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi gōngsī dǎobì ér shīyè le.
examples.english: He lost his job because the company went under.

examples.hanzi: 失业以后，他一直在找新工作。
examples.pinyin: Shīyè yǐhòu, tā yìzhí zài zhǎo xīn gōngzuò.
examples.english: After losing his job, he has been looking for a new one.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 香 originally combined grain with 甘 (sweet): the smell of cooked grain, in modern writing 日 stands in for 甘.
火 (fire) — 火 is fire, as in 烧, 灯, 炒; 烟 is smoke.
因 (yīn) — near sound — 烟 is yān; 因 also sounds out 姻 yīn.

example.hanzi: 医生建议他尽快戒掉香烟。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì tā jǐnkuài jièdiào xiāngyān.
example.english: The doctor advised him to quit cigarettes as soon as possible.
example.fact: The 1964 report of the U.S. Surgeon General was the first major government document to formally conclude that cigarette smoking causes lung cancer, drawing on over 7,000 studies reviewed by an advisory committee. It led directly to mandatory warning labels on cigarette packages in 1965 and reshaped decades of public health policy worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 公共场所不能抽香烟。
examples.pinyin: Gōnggòng chǎngsuǒ bù néng chōu xiāngyān.
examples.english: You can't smoke cigarettes in public places.

examples.hanzi: 他每天要抽一包香烟。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi tiān yào chōu yì bāo xiāngyān.
examples.english: He smokes a pack of cigarettes every day.

components.note: 毛 (hair, fur) — hair and fine things: 毯 blanket, 尾 tail; 毫 is fine hair, then a tiny amount, as in 毫米 millimeter.
高 (gāo) is only a loose sound hint for háo.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.

example.hanzi: 面对困难，他毫不犹豫地站了出来。
example.pinyin: Miànduì kùnnán, tā háobù yóuyù de zhànle chūlái.
example.english: Facing difficulty, he stepped forward without any hesitation.
example.fact: Gold leaf can be hammered so thin, down to around 100 nanometers, that light actually passes through it with a faint greenish tint, a thickness roughly a thousand times finer than a human hair. Traditional goldbeaters achieve this by repeatedly pounding and folding the metal between layers of specially treated parchment.

examples.hanzi: 他毫不在意别人的看法。
examples.pinyin: Tā háobù zàiyì biéren de kànfǎ.
examples.english: He doesn't care at all about what others think.

examples.hanzi: 她毫不犹豫地答应了。
examples.pinyin: Tā háobù yóuyù de dāyìng le.
examples.english: She agreed without the slightest hesitation.

components.note: 丬 (bed/couch, left side) — the left strip, a bed seen sideways. Dictionary story: going to bed at night, the 'future' that is sure to come; read as a memory aid.
夕 (evening) — upper part of the right side, as in 外 and 多; with 寸 (hand/inch) it frames 将 meaning 'about to / will'.
要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.

example.hanzi: 这座桥将要在明年完工。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo jiāngyào zài míngnián wángōng.
example.english: This bridge is going to be completed next year.
example.fact: Astronomers calculate that in roughly five billion years, the Sun will exhaust the hydrogen fuel in its core and swell into a red giant large enough to engulf Mercury and Venus, and possibly reach as far as Earth's orbit. Long before that, in about a billion years, rising solar luminosity is expected to boil away Earth's oceans entirely.

examples.hanzi: 电影将要开始了，请关掉手机。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng jiāngyào kāishǐ le, qǐng guān diào shǒujī.
examples.english: The movie is about to begin, so please turn off your phone.

examples.hanzi: 我们将要搬到另一座城市。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiāngyào bān dào lìng yí zuò chéngshì.
examples.english: We are going to move to another city.

components.note: 门 (mén, gate) is a close sound clue for wèn; the picture is asking at a gate, as in 闻 wén.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 吃, 唱, 叫: asking is a mouth action.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.hanzi: 见到老师，别忘了问好。
example.pinyin: Jiàndào lǎoshī, bié wàngle wènhǎo.
example.english: When you see the teacher, don't forget to say hello.
example.fact: Each of NASA's two Voyager probes, launched in 1977, carries a golden phonograph record containing spoken greetings in 55 different human languages, along with music, natural sounds, and images of Earth, intended as a message to any intelligent life that might one day encounter the spacecraft. Both Voyagers have since left the heliosphere and are now traveling through interstellar space.

examples.hanzi: 请替我向你的家人问好。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng tì wǒ xiàng nǐ de jiārén wènhǎo.
examples.english: Please say hello to your family for me.

examples.hanzi: 他每次见到我都会问好。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi cì jiàndào wǒ dōu huì wènhǎo.
examples.english: He greets me every time he sees me.

components.note: 隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: a strange feeling.
圣 here is not the "sage" word; it is only a loose sound clue for guài.

example.hanzi: 他昨晚没睡好，难怪今天这么累。
example.pinyin: Tā zuówǎn méi shuìhǎo, nánguài jīntiān zhème lèi.
example.english: He didn't sleep well last night, no wonder he's so tired today.
example.fact: In clinical trials, patients given a completely inactive sugar pill, but told it is a real painkiller, often report measurable reductions in pain, a phenomenon known as the placebo effect. Brain imaging studies have found that placebos can trigger the release of the body's own natural painkillers, called endorphins, which helps explain why patients sometimes genuinely feel better with no active drug at all.

examples.hanzi: 难怪他这么高兴，原来中奖了。
examples.pinyin: Nánguài tā zhème gāoxìng, yuánlái zhòngjiǎng le.
examples.english: No wonder he is so happy, he won a prize.

examples.hanzi: 外面下雪了，难怪这么冷。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn xiàxuě le, nánguài zhème lěng.
examples.english: It's snowing outside, no wonder it's so cold.

components.note: 兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.
月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.

example.hanzi: 团队最终克服了所有困难。
example.pinyin: Tuánduì zuìzhōng kèfúle suǒyǒu kùnnán.
example.english: The team ultimately overcame all the difficulties.
example.fact: When an oxygen tank exploded aboard Apollo 13 in April 1970, the three astronauts and mission control in Houston had to improvise a series of workarounds, including building a makeshift carbon dioxide filter out of a plastic bag, cardboard, and duct tape, to survive the four-day trip back to Earth. All three astronauts returned safely, and the mission is often cited as one of NASA's greatest examples of problem-solving under pressure.

examples.hanzi: 你要克服对水的恐惧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào kèfú duì shuǐ de kǒngjù.
examples.english: You need to overcome your fear of water.

examples.hanzi: 我们必须克服语言上的困难。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bìxū kèfú yǔyán shàng de kùnnán.
examples.english: We must overcome the language difficulties.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.

example.hanzi: 快递员上门送包裹。
example.pinyin: Kuàidìyuán shàngmén sòng bāoguǒ.
example.english: The delivery worker came to the door to deliver the package.
example.fact: Amazon's first drone delivery, Prime Air, dropped a package at a customer's door in Cambridge, England in December 2016, just 13 minutes after the order was placed. Modern last-mile delivery networks now route hundreds of millions of packages a day, and doorstep delivery has become the default retail experience in many countries.

examples.hanzi: 周末我想去奶奶家上门看看她。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ xiǎng qù nǎinai jiā shàngmén kànkan tā.
examples.english: This weekend I want to drop in on Grandma.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司提供上门维修服务。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī tígōng shàngmén wéixiū fúwù.
examples.english: This company offers on-site repair service.

components.note: 玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.hanzi: 医生对病人进行了全面检查。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng duì bìngrén jìnxíng le quánmiàn jiǎnchá.
example.english: The doctor gave the patient a comprehensive examination.
example.fact: The annual physical exam traces back to 19th-century life insurance companies, which required medical checkups to assess risk before issuing policies. Today, comprehensive full-body MRI screening is being studied as a way to catch early-stage cancers, though its cost-effectiveness for healthy populations is still debated among physicians.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要全面了解这个问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào quánmiàn liǎojiě zhège wèntí.
examples.english: We need a comprehensive understanding of this problem.

examples.hanzi: 这份报告全面总结了今年的工作。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn bàogào quánmiàn zǒngjié le jīnnián de gōngzuò.
examples.english: This report gives a full summary of this year's work.

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — marks birds, as in 鸭 duck, 鹅 goose, 鸽 pigeon; 鸡 is a chicken. 又 only replaces the old sound part.
尸 (body) — a body with 毛 fur behind it is a tail; 尸 also in 屁, 尿 and 层.
毛 (hair, fur) — the furry tip hanging off the back.
酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks and flavors: 醉 drunk, 醒 sober, 酸 sour, 配 match; 酒 is liquor, with 氵 for the liquid.
酉 also hints at the sound: yǒu is close to jiǔ.

example.hanzi: 他在酒吧点了一杯鸡尾酒。
example.pinyin: Tā zài jiǔbā diǎn le yì bēi jīwěijiǔ.
example.english: He ordered a cocktail at the bar.
example.fact: The Manhattan cocktail is said to have been invented in the 1870s at the Manhattan Club in New York City, possibly for a banquet hosted by Winston Churchill's mother, Jennie Jerome. The word 'cocktail' itself first appeared in print in a 1798 British newspaper, though its exact origin is still disputed by etymologists.

examples.hanzi: 这杯鸡尾酒是用橙汁和朗姆酒调的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bēi jīwěijiǔ shì yòng chéngzhī hé lǎngmǔjiǔ tiáo de.
examples.english: This cocktail is made with orange juice and rum.

examples.hanzi: 晚会上提供各种鸡尾酒和小点心。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnhuì shàng tígōng gèzhǒng jīwěijiǔ hé xiǎo diǎnxīn.
examples.english: The party serves all kinds of cocktails and snacks.

meanings: button (one that can be pressed to trigger an action)

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 按 is to press with the hand, as in 按摩 massage.
安 (ān) — same sound, different tone — 按 is àn; 安 also sounds out 案 àn.
钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metal radical; a button or knob, as in 钱 money, 铁 iron.
丑 (chǒu) is a loose sound clue; 扭 niǔ and 纽 niǔ share it and sound exactly like 钮.

example.hanzi: 请按下红色按钮启动机器。
example.pinyin: Qǐng ànxià hóngsè ànniǔ qǐdòng jīqì.
example.english: Please press the red button to start the machine.
example.fact: The international safety standard IEC 60947-5-5 requires emergency-stop buttons to be red, mushroom-shaped, and mounted on a yellow background so operators can find them instantly under stress. The design has barely changed since factory automation became widespread in the mid-20th century.

examples.hanzi: 电梯里的按钮坏了。
examples.pinyin: Diàntī lǐ de ànniǔ huài le.
examples.english: The button in the elevator is broken.

examples.hanzi: 你按一下这个按钮就行。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ àn yíxià zhège ànniǔ jiù xíng.
examples.english: Just press this button once.

components.note: 走 (run, walk) — movement: 起 rise, 越 cross, 赶 hurry, 趣; 超 is to jump over, surpass.
召 (zhào) is a loose sound clue; same part in 招 zhāo, 绍 shào, 照 zhào.
巾 (cloth) — cloth family: 布, 带, 帽. Memory aid: a market stall with a cloth banner 巾 under a roof 亠, i.e. a 市 market.
柿 (shì, persimmon) — contains 市 as a sound part, same sound shì.

example.hanzi: 妈妈每周去超市买菜。
example.pinyin: Māma měi zhōu qù chāoshì mǎi cài.
example.english: Mom goes to the supermarket every week to buy groceries.
example.fact: The world's first self-service supermarket, Piggly Wiggly, opened in Memphis, Tennessee in 1916, letting customers pick items off the shelves themselves instead of having a clerk fetch them. The change cut labor costs dramatically and became the template for grocery stores worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 超市里的水果今天打八折。
examples.pinyin: Chāoshì lǐ de shuǐguǒ jīntiān dǎ bā zhé.
examples.english: Fruit at the supermarket is 20% off today.

examples.hanzi: 我去超市买了一些牛奶和面包。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù chāoshì mǎi le yìxiē niúnǎi hé miànbāo.
examples.english: I went to the supermarket and bought some milk and bread.

components.note: 正 (zhèng, straight) with 不 not: not straight, so crooked, as in 歪斜.

example.hanzi: 墙上的画挂歪了。
example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng de huà guà wāi le.
example.english: The picture on the wall is hung crooked.
example.fact: 歪 is often a result complement: 写歪了 (written crooked), 坐歪了. Figuratively, 歪理 is twisted reasoning and 歪主意 is a bad idea. The idiom 歪打正着 means getting the right result by a lucky accident.

examples.hanzi: 他坐得歪歪的，很不舒服。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò de wāiwāi de, hěn bù shūfu.
examples.english: He is sitting crooked and very uncomfortable.

examples.hanzi: 你的帽子戴歪了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de màozi dài wāi le.
examples.english: Your hat is on crooked.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 探 is to reach out and feel, then to explore.
The right half is a sound part shared with 深 shēn: a loose clue for tàn.
糸 (thread, traditional of 纟) — silk and cord: 紧 tight, 系 tie; 索 is a twisted rope, seen in 线索 clue.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 他是一位勇敢的探索者。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi yǒnggǎn de tànsuǒzhě.
example.english: He is a brave explorer.
example.fact: Explorer 1, launched by the United States in January 1958, was the first American satellite to reach orbit, and it discovered the Van Allen radiation belts — bands of charged particles trapped by Earth's magnetic field. Physicist James Van Allen made the discovery using a simple Geiger counter aboard the satellite, one of the first major scientific results of the Space Age.

examples.hanzi: 探索者们在沙漠中发现了古城遗迹。
examples.pinyin: Tànsuǒzhěmen zài shāmò zhōng fāxiàn le gǔchéng yíjì.
examples.english: The explorers found the ruins of an ancient city in the desert.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们都是好奇的探索者。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen dōu shì hàoqí de tànsuǒzhě.
examples.english: Children are all curious explorers.

components.note: 两 (liǎng) — two, a pair; as a part it sounds out 辆 liàng and 俩 liǎ.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 两者之间没有明显的区别。
example.pinyin: Liǎngzhě zhī jiān méiyǒu míngxiǎn de qūbié.
example.english: There is no obvious difference between the two of them.
example.fact: Light behaves as both a wave and a particle, a duality confirmed by the double-slit experiment first performed with light by Thomas Young in 1801 and later shown to hold even for individual photons and electrons. Neither description alone is complete — physicists still rely on both models depending on which phenomenon they need to predict.

examples.hanzi: 红茶和绿茶，两者我都喜欢。
examples.pinyin: Hóngchá hé lǜchá, liǎngzhě wǒ dōu xǐhuan.
examples.english: Black tea and green tea, I like both.

examples.hanzi: 你只能选其中一个，不能两者都要。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhǐ néng xuǎn qízhōng yí ge, bù néng liǎngzhě dōu yào.
examples.english: You can only pick one, you can't have both.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; counting aloud.
十 (ten) — counting up to ten: 计 is to count and reckon.
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔 pen, 等 wait, 第: counting rods were once bamboo.
具 (jù, tool) — here the lower part shows hands holding the counting tools.

example.hanzi: 这台电脑可以快速计算复杂的数据。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái diànnǎo kěyǐ kuàisù jìsuàn fùzá de shùjù.
example.english: This computer can quickly calculate complex data.
example.fact: The Antikythera mechanism, recovered from a Greek shipwreck in 1901, is a hand-cranked bronze device built around 150-100 BC that could predict eclipses and track the positions of the sun, moon, and planets — historians consider it the world's oldest known analog computer.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我计算一下这顿饭的总价。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ jìsuàn yíxià zhè dùn fàn de zǒngjià.
examples.english: Please help me calculate the total price of this meal.

examples.hanzi: 他早就计算好了回家的时间。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǎo jiù jìsuàn hǎo le huíjiā de shíjiān.
examples.english: He had already worked out when to get home.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
爵 (wine cup) — 爵 was an ancient three-legged bronze wine cup, a mark of rank — so a noble title, as in 公爵.

example.hanzi: 他被国王封为公爵。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi guówáng fēng wéi gōngjué.
example.english: He was made a duke by the king.
example.fact: The title 'duke' derives from the Latin 'dux,' meaning military leader, originally given to Roman provincial commanders. In the United Kingdom today, only a handful of non-royal dukedoms remain, and the rank still sits just below the monarch and above every other hereditary peerage.

examples.hanzi: 公爵住在一座古老的城堡里。
examples.pinyin: Gōngjué zhù zài yí zuò gǔlǎo de chéngbǎo lǐ.
examples.english: The duke lived in an ancient castle.

examples.hanzi: 这部小说讲的是一位年轻公爵的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù xiǎoshuō jiǎng de shì yí wèi niánqīng gōngjué de gùshi.
examples.english: This novel tells the story of a young duke.

meanings: variant of 收穫|收获[shou1 huo4]

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.
艹 (grass) — the plant radical, as in 花 flower and 草 grass; it points to crops and harvest, the sense in 收获. Simplified 获 replaces 獲's left side with 艹.
犾 (dog-like part) — a variant of 犬 dog; 獲 originally meant catching game. Memory aid: grass plus a hunting dog, you bring something home.

example.hanzi: 农民在秋天收获稻子。
example.pinyin: Nóngmín zài qiūtiān shōuhuò dàozi.
example.english: Farmers harvest rice in the autumn.
example.fact: The mechanical combine harvester, invented in the United States in the 1830s, let a single machine cut, thresh, and clean grain in one pass — a task that had previously required dozens of laborers with scythes. Modern combines can harvest an acre of wheat in under six minutes.

examples.hanzi: 今年的苹果收获很好。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián de píngguǒ shōuhuò hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This year's apple harvest is very good.

examples.hanzi: 这次旅行让我收获了很多。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng ràng wǒ shōuhuò le hěn duō.
examples.english: I gained a lot from this trip.

components.note: 疒 (illness) — marks diseases and cravings, as in 病 sick, 痛 pain.
隐 (yǐn) gives the exact sound; it also means hidden, like a hidden craving.
尹 (to govern, a hand holding a staff) — the ruler; also in 伊 and 群 qún.
口 (mouth) — the ruler issues commands; 君 also sounds out 群 qún and 裙 qún.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 那个瘾君子已经戒毒三年了。
example.pinyin: Nàge yǐnjūnzǐ yǐjīng jièdú sān nián le.
example.english: That addict has been drug-free for three years now.
example.fact: In the 1970s, psychologist Bruce Alexander's 'Rat Park' experiment found that rats given free access to morphine-laced water used it far less when housed in a stimulating, social enclosure than rats isolated in bare cages — suggesting that environment and social connection play a major role in compulsive drug use, not the drug's chemistry alone.

examples.hanzi: 他以前是个瘾君子，现在已经改掉了坏习惯。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐqián shì ge yǐnjūnzǐ, xiànzài yǐjīng gǎidiào le huài xíguàn.
examples.english: He used to be an addict, but now he has kicked the bad habit.

examples.hanzi: 医生耐心帮助那位瘾君子重新生活。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng nàixīn bāngzhù nà wèi yǐnjūnzǐ chóngxīn shēnghuó.
examples.english: The doctor patiently helped that addict start a new life.

components.note: 奇 (qí) is a sound clue for 骑 qí, 寄 jì, 椅 yǐ and 崎 qí; as a word it means strange or remarkable.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women, as in 妈, 姐; 妙 first meant fine and delicate.
少 (shǎo) — loose hint — 妙 is miào; 少 also means few or little.

example.hanzi: 大自然充满了奇妙的现象。
example.pinyin: Dàzìrán chōngmǎn le qímiào de xiànxiàng.
example.english: Nature is full of marvelous phenomena.
example.fact: Bioluminescent plankton called dinoflagellates emit a ghostly blue glow when disturbed by waves or swimmers, a chemical reaction that likely evolved as a defense to startle predators or attract the predator's own predators. Beaches in the Maldives and parts of Australia are famous for these glowing 'sea sparkle' tides.

examples.hanzi: 宇宙真是太奇妙了。
examples.pinyin: Yǔzhòu zhēn shì tài qímiào le.
examples.english: The universe is truly amazing.

examples.hanzi: 孩子对世界充满了奇妙的想象。
examples.pinyin: Háizi duì shìjiè chōngmǎn le qímiào de xiǎngxiàng.
examples.english: Children are full of wonderful ideas about the world.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: water draining away.
肖 (xiāo) gives the exact sound; also in 销 xiāo and 削 xuē.
阝 on the left is 阜 (steps, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: 除 first meant palace steps; to step away, remove.
余 (yú) is a loose sound clue for chú; 余 also in 涂 tú, 途 tú and 徐 xú.

example.hanzi: 疫苗帮助消除了许多传染病。
example.pinyin: Yìmiáo bāngzhù xiāochú le xǔduō chuánrǎnbìng.
example.english: Vaccines have helped eliminate many infectious diseases.
example.fact: Smallpox is the only human disease ever fully eradicated, declared eliminated worldwide by the World Health Organization in 1980 after a global vaccination campaign. The last natural case occurred in Somalia in 1977, and the virus now exists only in two high-security laboratories, in the United States and Russia.

examples.hanzi: 这种药能消除疼痛。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào néng xiāochú téngtòng.
examples.english: This medicine can relieve pain.

examples.hanzi: 聊天帮他消除了紧张。
examples.pinyin: Liáotiān bāng tā xiāochú le jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: Chatting helped him get rid of his nervousness.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house or shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 完; a hand 寸 under a roof means guarding.
寸 (hand, inch) — originally a hand, as in 对, 寻, 封.
乛 (hook stroke) — the top-left bent stroke and dictionary radical; a stroke grouping with no meaning of its own.
一 (one) — the bottom bar. 卫 is simplified from 衛 (guard); Memory aid: a bar blocking a corner, a guard at the door.

example.hanzi: 士兵在城门口守卫。
example.pinyin: Shìbīng zài chéngmén kǒu shǒuwèi.
example.english: The soldiers guard the city gate.
example.fact: The Terracotta Army, buried around 210 BC to guard the tomb of China's first emperor Qin Shi Huang, consists of over 8,000 life-sized clay soldiers, each with individually sculpted facial features. It was discovered by farmers digging a well in 1974 near Xi'an.

examples.hanzi: 狗在门口守卫着房子。
examples.pinyin: Gǒu zài ménkǒu shǒuwèi zhe fángzi.
examples.english: The dog guards the house at the door.

examples.hanzi: 他是守卫球门的守门员。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì shǒuwèi qiúmén de shǒuményuán.
examples.english: He is the goalkeeper who defends the goal.

components.note: 日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 你是不是忘记带伞了?
example.pinyin: Nǐ shì bu shì wàngjì dài sǎn le?
example.english: Did you forget to bring an umbrella?
example.fact: Transport for London's lost-property office reports collecting tens of thousands of umbrellas in a single year across the city's transit system — more than almost any other item besides phones and keys, according to its annual reports.

examples.hanzi: 你是不是不舒服？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì bu shì bù shūfu?
examples.english: Aren't you feeling well?

examples.hanzi: 这是不是你的手机？
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì bu shì nǐ de shǒujī?
examples.english: Is this your phone?

meanings: to act on behalf of sb in a responsible position
to act as an agent or proxy

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 代 is one person replacing another, then a generation.
弋 (yì) is only a loose hint; 代 itself sounds out 袋 dài and 贷 dài.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 他委托律师代理这场官司。
example.pinyin: Tā wěituō lǜshī dàilǐ zhè chǎng guānsī.
example.english: He appointed a lawyer to act as his representative in the lawsuit.
example.fact: In computer networking, a proxy server sits between a user and the internet, forwarding requests on the user's behalf — a concept first widely implemented in the early 1990s to cache web pages and speed up slow dial-up connections, long before it became a common tool for privacy and content filtering.

examples.hanzi: 经理不在时，由他代理工作。
examples.pinyin: Jīnglǐ bú zài shí, yóu tā dàilǐ gōngzuò.
examples.english: When the manager is away, he handles the work on his behalf.

examples.hanzi: 这家店代理多个品牌的手机。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn dàilǐ duō ge pǐnpái de shǒujī.
examples.english: This shop is an agent for several phone brands.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家, 室; 牢 is a pen with a roof for cattle 牛, then a prison.
牛 (ox) — 牛 is cattle — kept inside for safety, so firm.
户 (door) — doors and houses, as in 所 and 扇: a room with a door.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fáng; 方 also sounds out 放 fàng and 访 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 犯人被关在狭小的牢房里。
example.pinyin: Fànrén bèi guān zài xiáxiǎo de láofáng lǐ.
example.english: The prisoner was locked in a cramped jail cell.
example.fact: Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary in San Francisco Bay, which operated from 1934 to 1963, was considered virtually escape-proof due to the cold, fast currents around the island. In 1962 three inmates famously escaped using papier-mâché head decoys, and their fate remains officially unresolved to this day.

examples.hanzi: 警察把他带进了牢房。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá bǎ tā dàijìn le láofáng.
examples.english: The police took him into a cell.

examples.hanzi: 牢房里又冷又暗。
examples.pinyin: Láofáng lǐ yòu lěng yòu àn.
examples.english: The cell was cold and dark.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.

example.hanzi: 良好的天气对比赛非常有利。
example.pinyin: Liánghǎo de tiānqì duì bǐsài fēicháng yǒulì.
example.english: Good weather is very advantageous for the competition.
example.fact: Marathon world records are almost always set on flat, cool courses with a slight tailwind, since even a small elevation gain or headwind measurably slows runners. That's why pancake-flat cities like Berlin and Chicago have hosted far more record-breaking marathons than hillier cities like Boston.

examples.hanzi: 早睡早起对身体有利。
examples.pinyin: Zǎo shuì zǎo qǐ duì shēntǐ yǒulì.
examples.english: Going to bed and rising early is good for your health.

examples.hanzi: 这个消息对我们很有利。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi duì wǒmen hěn yǒulì.
examples.english: This news is very favorable for us.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — arranging and moving by hand: 打, 推, 拉; 排 is to line things up.
非 (fēi) is a loose sound hint; its series includes 悲 bēi and 菲 fēi.
阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 队 is a group of people gathered together.

example.hanzi: 大家都在排队买票。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu zài páiduì mǎi piào.
example.english: Everyone is lining up to buy tickets.
example.fact: Queueing theory, the mathematical study of waiting lines, was pioneered by Danish engineer Agner Krarup Erlang in 1909 while analyzing telephone traffic at the Copenhagen Telephone Company. His formulas are still used today to design call centers, hospital triage systems, and amusement park ride lines.

examples.hanzi: 请在黄线后面排队等候。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài huángxiàn hòumiàn páiduì děnghòu.
examples.english: Please wait in line behind the yellow line.

examples.hanzi: 早上银行门口已经排队了。
examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang yínháng ménkǒu yǐjīng páiduì le.
examples.english: People were already lining up at the bank in the morning.

components.note: 要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.

example.hanzi: 快点走,要不然我们会迟到。
example.pinyin: Kuài diǎn zǒu, yàobùrán wǒmen huì chídào.
example.english: Hurry up, or else we'll be late.
example.fact: Tokyo's train system is famous for its punctuality, with average delays measured in seconds rather than minutes. In 2017 a train operator publicly apologized after a train departed 20 seconds early, a small illustration of how tightly the country's rail schedules are run compared to systems elsewhere.

examples.hanzi: 多穿点衣服，要不然会感冒的。
examples.pinyin: Duō chuān diǎn yīfu, yàobùrán huì gǎnmào de.
examples.english: Wear more clothes, otherwise you'll catch a cold.

examples.hanzi: 你要不然就回家休息吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yàobùrán jiù huíjiā xiūxi ba.
examples.english: Or else you could just go home and rest.

components.note: 厂 (shelter) — 厂 stands for a building or shelter, as here — 厨 is the room where food is cooked, in 厨房 kitchen and 厨师 chef.
师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.hanzi: 这位厨师做的菜非常美味。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi chúshī zuò de cài fēicháng měiwèi.
example.english: The dishes this chef makes are extremely delicious.
example.fact: The tall, pleated white hat traditionally worn by chefs, the toque, is said to date to the 16th century, when cooks fleeing religious persecution in the Byzantine Empire hid in Orthodox monasteries and adopted the tall hats worn by monks. The hat's height later became a way to signal rank, with head chefs wearing taller toques than junior cooks.

examples.hanzi: 这家饭店的厨师是从广东来的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā fàndiàn de chúshī shì cóng Guǎngdōng lái de.
examples.english: This restaurant's chef is from Guangdong.

examples.hanzi: 我哥哥想当一名厨师。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge xiǎng dāng yì míng chúshī.
examples.english: My older brother wants to become a chef.

components.note: 欠 (open mouth, yawn) — breath and mouth actions, as in 歌 song, 吹 blow, 欢 happy.
曷 (hé) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 喝 hē and 渴 kě.

example.hanzi: 累了就歇一会儿吧。
example.pinyin: Lèi le jiù xiē yíhuìr ba.
example.english: If you are tired, take a little rest.
example.fact: 歇 is a colloquial, mostly northern word for taking a break: 歇一歇, 歇脚 (to stop and rest the feet). 歇业 means a shop closes, and 歇后语 is a two-part folk saying where the punch line is left unsaid.

examples.hanzi: 你先歇一会儿，我来做饭。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān xiē yíhuìr, wǒ lái zuò fàn.
examples.english: Take a rest first, and I will cook.

examples.hanzi: 商店今天歇业，明天再来吧。
examples.pinyin: Shāngdiàn jīntiān xiēyè, míngtiān zài lái ba.
examples.english: The shop is closed today, so come back tomorrow.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 喘 is panting, breathing hard.
耑 (zhuān) — loose sound hint (chuǎn); same part in 端 duān and 湍 tuān.

example.hanzi: 他跑得太快，喘不过气来。
example.pinyin: Tā pǎo de tài kuài, chuǎn bu guò qì lái.
example.english: He ran so fast that he could not catch his breath.
example.fact: 喘气 means to breathe hard or just "to catch a breath": 喘口气. 哮喘 and 气喘 refer to asthma. 喘不过气 is also used figuratively when pressure feels overwhelming.

examples.hanzi: 爬完山，他累得直喘气。
examples.pinyin: Pá wán shān, tā lèi de zhí chuǎnqì.
examples.english: After climbing the mountain, he was panting with exhaustion.

examples.hanzi: 他有哮喘，不能跑太快。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu xiàochuǎn, bù néng pǎo tài kuài.
examples.english: He has asthma and cannot run too fast.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — giving by hand; also in 给 give, 拿 take.
肙 (yuān) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 娟 juān and 鹃 juān.
贝 (shell, old money) — gifts and valuables, as in 财 wealth, 买 buy, 费 fee.
曾 (zēng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 增 zēng and 憎 zēng.

example.hanzi: 他捐赠了大量资金给医院。
example.pinyin: Tā juānzèng le dàliàng zījīn gěi yīyuàn.
example.english: He donated a large sum of money to the hospital.
example.fact: The Giving Pledge, launched by Warren Buffett and Bill and Melinda Gates in 2010, asks billionaires to commit at least half their wealth to charity, either during their lifetime or in their will. As of the mid-2020s, more than 200 individuals and families across over 20 countries had signed on.

examples.hanzi: 很多人向灾区捐赠衣物。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō rén xiàng zāiqū juānzèng yīwù.
examples.english: Many people donated clothing to the disaster area.

examples.hanzi: 她把自己的书捐赠给了图书馆。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zìjǐ de shū juānzèng gěi le túshūguǎn.
examples.english: She donated her books to the library.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person's precedent or example; also in 他 he, 做 do.
列 (liè) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 烈 liè and 裂 liè.
女 (woman) — women and family terms, as in 妈 mom, 好 good, 姐 sister; 女 (nǚ) also loosely echoes the rú sound.
口 (mouth) — speech; 如 originally meant "to follow, accord with", later "as, like"; also in 汝 rǔ and 茹 rú.

example.hanzi: 许多水果,例如苹果和香蕉,都富含维生素。
example.pinyin: Xǔduō shuǐguǒ, lìrú píngguǒ hé xiāngjiāo, dōu fùhán wéishēngsù.
example.english: Many fruits, for example apples and bananas, are rich in vitamins.
example.fact: Scurvy, caused by vitamin C deficiency, plagued sailors on long ocean voyages for centuries until Scottish physician James Lind ran one of the first controlled clinical trials in 1747, proving that citrus fruits like limes and lemons could cure and prevent it — decades before vitamins were even understood as a concept.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢吃水果，例如西瓜和葡萄。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chī shuǐguǒ, lìrú xīguā hé pútáo.
examples.english: I like fruit, for example watermelon and grapes.

examples.hanzi: 有些运动很适合冬天，例如滑雪。
examples.pinyin: Yǒuxiē yùndòng hěn shìhé dōngtiān, lìrú huáxuě.
examples.english: Some sports suit winter well, such as skiing.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 扮 is to dress or act.
分 (fēn) — loose hint — 扮 is bàn; 分 also sounds out 盼 pàn.

example.hanzi: 他在戏里扮演一个老人。
example.pinyin: Tā zài xì lǐ bànyǎn yí ge lǎorén.
example.english: In the play he acts as an old man.
example.fact: 扮 appears in 扮演 (to play a role), 打扮 (to dress up, very common), 假扮 (to pose as) and 扮鬼脸 (to make faces). 打扮 describes making yourself look good, not just changing clothes.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们扮成小动物去表演。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen bàn chéng xiǎo dòngwù qù biǎoyǎn.
examples.english: The children dressed up as little animals to perform.

examples.hanzi: 她今天打扮得很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān dǎban de hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: She is dressed up beautifully today.

components.note: 冬 — the last season of the year; in old script it is related to 终 zhōng "end", as winter ends the year.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.hanzi: 北方的冬天非常寒冷。
example.pinyin: Běifāng de dōngtiān fēicháng hánlěng.
example.english: Winters in the north are extremely cold.
example.fact: The coldest inhabited place on Earth is the Siberian town of Oymyakon, Russia, where temperatures have dropped as low as -67.7°C (-89.9°F). Despite this, around 500 people still live there year-round, keeping their cars running constantly since engines can crack if turned off in the deep winter.

examples.hanzi: 冬天我喜欢喝热茶。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān wǒ xǐhuan hē rè chá.
examples.english: In winter I like drinking hot tea.

examples.hanzi: 今年冬天特别冷，还下了大雪。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián dōngtiān tèbié lěng, hái xià le dà xuě.
examples.english: This winter is especially cold, and there was heavy snow.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.hanzi: 婚礼上的场面十分壮观。
example.pinyin: Hūnlǐ shàng de chǎngmiàn shífēn zhuàngguān.
example.english: The scene at the wedding was truly spectacular.
example.fact: The opening ceremony of the 2008 Beijing Olympics involved over 15,000 performers and featured a giant unrolling scroll made of LED screens. Directed by filmmaker Zhang Yimou, it remains one of the most expensive opening ceremonies in Olympic history, reportedly costing over $100 million.

examples.hanzi: 球场上的场面非常热闹。
examples.pinyin: Qiúchǎng shàng de chǎngmiàn fēicháng rènao.
examples.english: The scene at the stadium was very lively.

examples.hanzi: 面对尴尬的场面，他笑了笑。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì gāngà de chǎngmiàn, tā xiào le xiào.
examples.english: Faced with the awkward situation, he just smiled.

meanings: to be in the prime of life

components.note: 當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).
年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.

example.hanzi: 当年他还只是一个学生。
example.pinyin: Dāngnián tā hái zhǐshì yí gè xuéshēng.
example.english: Back then, he was still just a student.
example.fact: The Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 lasted only 12 seconds and covered 120 feet, shorter than the wingspan of a modern Boeing 747. Just 66 years later, in 1969, humans landed on the Moon — a pace of change historians often cite as one of the fastest in human history.

examples.hanzi: 当年我们一起在这条街上长大。
examples.pinyin: Dāngnián wǒmen yìqǐ zài zhè tiáo jiē shàng zhǎngdà.
examples.english: Back then we grew up together on this street.

examples.hanzi: 他当年是班上最安静的孩子。
examples.pinyin: Tā dāngnián shì bān shàng zuì ānjìng de háizi.
examples.english: Back then he was the quietest kid in the class.

components.note: 纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — plain unmixed thread, hence pure; also in 红 red, 级 level.
屯 (tún) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 钝 dùn and 顿 dùn.
米 (rice, grain) — pure unmixed grain, hence essence; also in 粉 powder, 粮 grain.
卒 (zú) is a loose clue; it starts the cuì series 翠 cuì, 悴 cuì and 瘁 cuì.

example.hanzi: 这是纯粹的巧合。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì chúncuì de qiǎohé.
example.english: This is pure coincidence.
example.fact: Gold with a purity of 24 karats is considered 'pure gold,' containing no other metals, but because pure gold is very soft, jewelry is usually made with 18K or 14K gold alloyed with metals like copper or silver to increase durability and change its color slightly.

examples.hanzi: 他这么做纯粹是为了好玩。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhème zuò chúncuì shì wèile hǎowán.
examples.english: He did this purely for fun.

examples.hanzi: 这杯果汁是纯粹的，没有加糖。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bēi guǒzhī shì chúncuì de, méiyǒu jiā táng.
examples.english: This juice is pure, with no sugar added.
